subject: physics
title: Real Image
textbookText: Real Image An image formed due to the actual intersection of light rays after reflection or refraction is called real image. A real image can be obtained on a screen. The real image is inverted with respect to the object.
A virtual image is formed when the light rays after reflection or refraction do not actually
intersect but appear to intersect when produced backward. A virtual image cannot be obtained
on a screen. A virtual image is erected or upright with respect to the object.

Virtual image A virtual image is formed when light rays appear to converge at a point. A virtual image cannot be cast onto a screen. A virtual image is erected with respect to the object. Images formed in a plane mirror and aconvex mirror are examples of virtual images.
